set.t: Look for the old grove on the 1930s aerial. Private land: ask permission. The real 1868 Newton robbery: about $3,600-4,000 in greenbacks blown from the Jasper Co treasurer's safe on 25 Feb 1868; Pinkerton's H. W. Davis tracked four men who left by train west next morning, got off at Mitchellville and went on to Chicago, where Chas. Udell and Abram Richardson (the 'Abraham Ross' of March reports) were arrested; they got 10 and 7 years in Dec 1868. 'Of the $3,600 of which the county was robbed only $945 were recovered'; the others were never caught. About $2,650 was never recovered, but it was paper money, the flight ran east by rail, and no period record puts any of it near State Center.
set.tovw: Lead grade D: one secondary telling (Laird 1927); the 1868 robbery is real and ~$2,650 in greenbacks was never recovered, but nothing period ties it to the Skunk River grove

pinev: About 1.5 mi east of Livermore, behind a cabin on a later farm; also 'all along Bloody Run', the creek south of town

Bicknell (1897) fixes the local landmarks: Sidominadota's 1854 camp stood on the right bank of Bloody Run about half a mile SW of its mouth, on the A. B. Miner farm, about 80 rods NW of the house; Lott's whiskey cabin was east of the river opposite the mouth of Lott's Creek. This is the Lott affair, not the 1857 Johnson traders, but it places Bloody Run and the early whiskey trade in the same reach of the Des Moines below Livermore.
Humboldt Co papers are indexed from the 1890s; no telling of the Johnson traders, the hogsheads or Bloody Run gold appears before Laird's 1927 thesis.

tw-il-deerfield-schulz-jar-1920.st: On 4 Sep 1920 Mrs. Adolph Schultz (Glenview RFD) wrote to the News-Sun calling the 27 Aug story false and asking for 'a flat denial'; the Libertyville report had already noted the family's fear of a treasure-trove claim by the former owner, so the denial reads as protective.
